3.text: three thousand who are more or less sedentary, and of another three thousand

4.text: wandering natives; i.e., more than eight rubles per man. The total revenue

7.text: As a rule, the officials are sent to remote districts such as the Kolyma

8.text: either as punishment for some trespass, or they go tempted by the comparatively

9.text: high salary and the short term of service (ten years) necessary for a full

10.text: pension. They enjoy the full freedom of their administrative position, which

11.text: leads them very soon to indulge in excesses. After two or three years a

12.text: higher official is sent from Yakutsk to inspect and to verify the accounts.

13.text: This often ends either in the district official heavily bribing the inspector, or

14.text: in his being deprived of his position and impeached before the court. Fully

15.text: one half of the chief officials of the Kolyma have ended their careers and

16.text: even their lives while under impeachment. Some of them, too, have been

17.text: adventurers from the very beginning. Even criminals sent from European

18.text: Russia to Siberia have then been accepted again into service and sent as far

19.text: as the Kolyma. I may mention here Vinogradov, who was in service in the

20.text: thirties of the nineteenth century. In the year 1837 a member of the Provincial

21.text: Council, Ring, was sent to inspect his office. Almost immediately the two

22.text: got into a violent quarrel, which ended all of a sudden in the death of

23.text: Ring. Local tradition says that Vinogradov caused Ring to be poisoned; and

24.text: I have found in the Archives an order, directed by Vinogradov to the private

25.text: commander of the Cossacks of Nishne-Kolymsk, referring to the death of

26.text: Ring, and of rather doubtful significance. Another document referring to

27.text: 1839, when Vinogradov was dismissed and impeached before a court, mentions

28.text: his attempt to murder his wife, for which he was legally prosecuted. His

29.text: wife was the daughter of a local priest. He accused her of improper conduct,

30.text: “too improper even for the Kolyma,” as it is stated in the document. I might

31.text: mention more episodes of a similar character and of more recent date.

32.text: It is no wonder that the doings of such an Administration present forms

33.text: quite strange, to say the least. I will give a few instances. The inquiries

34.text: for all persons wanted by the courts or police throughout the immense empire

35.text: are sent, as a rule, to every district, however remote. Thus the mail, which

36.text: up to very recent times came only three times a year, would bring piles of

37.text: such orders, and all local archives are full of them: as, for example, the order

38.text: of the chief secretary of military affairs inquiring for the dismissed Lieut-Col.

39.text: von Stempel and his step-daughter Eugenie Krumones, in reference to their
